result: Arms and powder taken from the State House and two magazines, no fight
captured: About 800 muskets and other arms from the State House attic; about 1,600 lb of powder from the Hobcaw and Cochran's magazines
place: Charleston (State House, Broad and Meeting Streets)
coordinate_basis: Taken at town level from the infobox coordinate of the Siege of Charleston article (S121); the State House stood at the northwest corner of Broad and Meeting Streets (S117), about 2 km south-southeast of that point, and the powder magazines lay across the Cooper River (Hobcaw) and north of the town (Cochran's). To be read from a modern map.
notes: Cross-checked: S116 (list no. 1) and S117 (place, quantities). No second source gives the quantities.

result: Fort surrendered without a fight
coordinate_basis: Taken from the GPS of the Fort Charlotte memorial site on the lake shore (S126); the marker on Route 81 at Mt. Carmel (34.0059, -82.5072) says the ruins lie 6.6 miles southwest of it (HMdb 9185, S122). The ruins lie under the lake, so the true point is within about 2 km.
notes: Cross-checked: S116 (list no. 3), HMdb marker 9185 (Mayson seized it 12 Jul 1775; Whitfield surrendered it) (peaceful surrender).

result: Fort taken without a fight after the navy disabled its guns
captured: The fort (the British had disabled its guns)
coordinate_basis: The coordinates ABT gives for Fort Johnson (Fort Johnson Rd, northeast point of James Island, S120); Lipscomb places the fort on Windmill Point (S117).
notes: Cross-checked: S117 (the navy disabled the guns; Motte entered; three privates left; no fighting) and the ABT heritage-site page (Motte took it with little resistance). The ABT page gives no day; The Archives list gives 15 Sep.

result: Loyalists besiege Williamson's camp; a truce ends it
other_reading: The NPS timeline dates the siege 10-21 Nov 1775 and the park brochure puts the first attack on 18 Nov; the Archives list, Wikipedia and the NPS anniversary page say 19-21 Nov. All sources read agree on the result: no winner and a truce.
place: Savage's Old Field / Williamson's fort, Ninety Six
coordinate_basis: The knoll in Ninety Six National Historic Site where the 1775 stockade stood (NPS online tour stop 16 and the Colonials and Patriots survey, S128); Wikipedia's infobox coordinate for the site (S121); HMdb 30623 marker at 34.1469, -82.0232 (S122).
notes: Loss: Patriots 1 killed 12 wounded, Loyalists 4 killed 20 wounded (S121, citing Cann, SCHM 76, pp. 207-214). Date disagreement only; result agreed. Dagger on the date.

result: Loyalist camp surprised; about 130 taken
captured: About 130 Loyalists, with men, weapons and supplies
place: Great Cane Brake (Reedy River, near Simpsonville)
coordinate_basis: The marker stands at the Wikipedia coordinate (S121); the marker text puts the fight along the south side of a creek running to the Reedy River and its present place on Fork Shoals Road is not the original (HMdb 97258, S122). The exact ground is not known.
notes: Cross-checked: S116 (list no. 11), S125 and Wikipedia (5 or 6 Loyalists killed, 1 Patriot wounded, about 130 captured), S123 (Richardson entry: an unquestioned success).

result: Fort holds; the fleet fails to force the harbour
coordinate_basis: The coordinate of Fort Moultrie (S121, from NPS); the 1776 palmetto fort stood on Sullivan's Island at the harbour mouth (S119; Lipscomb S117).
notes: Cross-checked by S117, S119 (first decisive Patriot victory over the Royal Navy; British over 200 casualties, Americans 12 killed 26 wounded), S120 (American Victory) and S118. Ship mark: British ships.

result: Landing attempt stopped at the inlet
coordinate_basis: HMdb 67277 marker on Sullivan's Island at Breach Inlet, 32 46.487 N 79 48.868 W (S122); the American lines stood on the island side and the British camp on Long Island (Isle of Palms).
notes: Cross-checked: S119 (Clinton's flotilla could not cross against Thomson's fire; the inlet was far deeper than he believed), S117 (no usable ford), S120 (label American Victory; read from a search result only).

result: Ambush on Williamson's column; the Patriots recover and drive the force off (proposed)
other_reading: The NPS timeline says only that the Patriots were ambushed by Cherokees and rescued by a mounted charge, and the SC Encyclopedia says Cameron's force ambushed Williamson. ABT scores it an American victory.
coordinate_basis: The HMdb Seneca Town / Fort Rutledge marker near Clemson (34 40.013 N, 82 50.708 W, S122); the town lay on the east side of the Keowee River and is now under Lake Hartwell (ABT, Liberty Trail). The town's exact place is lost.
notes: PROPOSED reading only (ABT). Needs Opus: see SCH02. Black (Cherokee) is not drawn unless the other reading is adopted as a Cherokee win, which no source read says.

result: Pickens's ring holds until relief; the Cherokee flee and Tamassee is burned (proposed)
other_reading: ABT scores the Ring Fight inconclusive and the Liberty Trail says it had no victors; the SC Encyclopedia counts 65 Cherokee killed against 11 of Pickens's men.
coordinate_basis: The Tamassee Town marker at the road junction near the site (HMQ2V, 34 52.98 N 83 2.91 W; text: "near this site", S122).
notes: PROPOSED reading only. Not on Morgan's dagger list: this session found the disagreement. Needs Opus: see SCH03.

result: Moultrie beats a British detachment; it withdraws
place: Port Royal Island, near Gray's Hill
coordinate_basis: HMdb 14738 marker near the old halfway house at Gray's Hill (32 28.849 N 80 44.387 W, S122); the marker stands about 6 miles north of Beaufort (S122); Wikipedia gives 32.5003, -80.7436 (S121).
notes: Cross-checked: ABT American Victory (casualties not re-read), NPS timeline (Moultrie defeated a British detachment), SC Encyclopedia entry.

result: Prevost's advance on the city ends in a withdrawal
coordinate_basis: The infobox coordinate of the Siege of Charleston article (S121), used for the line of the city's defences; the British reached the lines on 11-12 May and were found gone on 13 May (S124, S118).
notes: No battle was won: the British broke off on 12-13 May when Lincoln was found to be returning (S118, S124). Drawn as an American success because the city held.

result: Lincoln's attack on the rear guard repulsed (proposed)
other_reading: The NPS timeline calls it inconclusive but costly to both sides; ABT scores it a British victory and the NPS siege article says Lincoln was repulsed.
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121) .
notes: PROPOSED reading only. Casualties (Wikipedia): Americans 34 killed, 113 wounded, 155 missing; British 26 killed, 93 wounded, 1 missing. Needs Opus: see SCH04.

result: City and army surrendered 12 May
captured: Charleston and the American army: about 5,000 men (5,266 to 5,466 by the figures Wikipedia gives), 311 guns, 49 ships and 120 boats
other_reading: Same result, different start date: ABT begins the siege on 11 Feb 1780 (the landing); the NPS timeline, Wikipedia and Mount Vernon begin it on 29 Mar (the crossing of the Ashley).
coordinate_basis: The infobox coordinate of the Siege of Charleston article (S121) (about the Neck and the lines of 1780); the city centre lies about 2 km south-southeast.
notes: Cross-checked by Britannica (Lincoln surrendered 12 May), NPS timeline, ABT map page and Wikipedia (Buchanan pp. 26-29; Borick p. 169; Mattern p. 101). Fort Moultrie surrendered 7 May without a fight. Ship mark: British fleet crossed the bar on 8 Apr. Date dagger only.

result: American cavalry and militia scattered before dawn
captured: 185 horses and 30 wagons of arms, powder, clothing and ammunition
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); ABT places it at Monck's Corner, Berkeley County.
notes: The "Not checked" row, now read: ABT (British Victory; American 15 killed, 18 wounded, 63 missing or captured; British 3 wounded) and Wikipedia (Ward 1952; Wilson 2005).

result: American cavalry surprised at the ferry and scattered
captured: About 100 horses, arms and equipment; 18 British prisoners freed
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate near Jamestown (S121); ABT places it at the crossing of the Santee River in Berkeley County.
notes: The "Not checked" row, now read: ABT (British Victory; about 41 American casualties, none British), Wikipedia (Buchanan pp. 68-69; Borick p. 193).

result: Buford's command destroyed
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate near Lancaster County (S121).
notes: Cross-checked: NPS (113 bayoneted), Wikipedia (113 killed, 150 wounded, 53 captured; Piecuch).

result: Sumter's attack fails; he withdraws (proposed)
captured: Nothing at the post; Sumter claimed about 60 Loyalists, a few horses and some supplies on the retreat
other_reading: Wikipedia dates the action 31 Jul or 1 Aug, against 30 Jul in the Archives list, the NPS timeline and ABT; the result agrees (British victory, ABT and Wikipedia; Sumter withdrew, NPS).
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121).
notes: Result as ABT (via Morgan's list) and Wikipedia: British victory. The captured-by line is Sumter's own claim as Morgan's list gives it. Date dagger.

result: Davie's raid on the Loyalist camp succeeds
captured: 60 horses and about 100 muskets and rifles
other_reading: Wikipedia dates Davie's raid 1 Aug; the Archives list, the NPS timeline and ABT (as a diversion for Rocky Mount) date it 30 Jul. Same result.
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate for the Hanging Rock action (S121); Davie's raid was on the Loyalist camp in the same district (ABT, Heath Springs).
notes: Date dagger only (SCH06). The quantities are as Morgan's list gives them (from the Archives list); Wikipedia says 60 horses and some weapons.

result: Heavy losses on both sides; Sumter leaves the field (proposed)
captured: About 100 horses, 250 stands of arms and 73 prisoners (Sumter's report, as ABT quotes it)
other_reading: NPS: Sumter inflicted heavy casualties but was forced to retreat; Wikipedia: American victory with the Americans leaving the field; ABT: American Victory though Sumter did not take the garrison.
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); ABT places it at the garrison on the Camden to Charlotte road at Heath Springs.
notes: PROPOSED reading only. Casualties (ABT): Americans 53, British 200; Sumter's own letter gives other figures. Needs Opus: see SCH07.

result: Gates's army routed
captured: All 8 American guns, over 200 wagons; about 1,000 prisoners (Cornwallis)
coordinate_basis: The coordinates ABT gives for the Camden battlefield (S120); Wikipedia 34.3646, -80.6139 (S121).
notes: The "Not checked" row, now read: ABT (British Victory; casualty figures not re-read), Wikipedia (Ramsay vol. 2 p. 169 for guns, wagons and baggage; Cornwallis to Germain, 21 Aug, for the prisoners).

result: Sumter's camp surprised and his command scattered
captured: About 300 American prisoners; wagons, artillery pieces, about 800 horses and about 1,000 weapons (ABT, as Morgan's list reads it); the British prisoners and baggage Sumter had taken
place: Fishing Creek, north of Great Falls
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121), north of Great Falls in Chester County.
notes: Cross-checked: NPS (Tarleton surprised and defeated Sumter), Wikipedia (British victory; about 300 captured; Pancake), Morgan's list for the ABT page (guns, horses, weapons counts not re-read).

result: Loyalist force ambushed and beaten; Patriots then withdraw
other_reading: Same result, two dates: 18 Aug (NPS, the Archives list, Wikipedia's infobox) against 19 Aug (ABT, Wikipedia's lead).
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate for the state historic site (S121).
notes: Loyalists 63 killed and 70 captured; Patriots 4 killed and 12 wounded (wayside, via Wikipedia). Edgar pp. 130-38; Buchanan pp. 177-179. Date dagger only.

result: Loyalist camp attacked at midnight and driven into the swamp
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate, given to the minute (S121).
notes: The attack came near midnight on 28/29 Sep (Wikipedia infobox 28, text 29; Crawford 2024 p. 116 for the date). Patriots 2 killed, 8 wounded.

result: Ferguson's force destroyed
captured: About 698 British and Loyalists missing and captured (ABT, via Morgan's list); Wikipedia gives 668 or 698
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); the battlefield is a National Military Park.
notes: Cross-checked: NPS (frontier militia surrounded and defeated Ferguson, a decisive Patriot victory), Wikipedia (the article cites Dameron and Buchanan; pages not recorded). The capture figures differ: 668 or 698.

result: Loyalist camp routed at midnight
coordinate_basis: The 1980 Clarendon County marker "near here" on North Brewington Road, Gable (33 48.854 N 80 8.556 W; HMdb 227712, S122); Clarendon County's own page gives 33.81444, -80.14289 (S126); Wikipedia 33.803, -80.125 (S121). The 2002 marker at Turbeville is 15 km north-east.
notes: Cross-checked: NPS (Marion routed Tynes), ABT (American Victory; 43 casualties, all Loyalist), carolana (6 killed, 14 wounded, 23 captured), HMdb. Boatner places it near where US 301 crosses the Black River.

result: Night attack on Sumter's camp fails; Wemyss wounded and taken
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); the Chester Rotary Club monument at 34 35.682 N 81 25.038 W (HMdb 13686, S122) and the state marker (13685) stand on the Chester side of the ford.
notes: Cross-checked: NPS (night attack failed), the marker (Sumter beat Wemyss), Wikipedia (about 1 a.m. 9 Nov) and carolana (Wemyss wounded and captured; Wikipedia: British lost 20 killed or wounded after about twenty minutes). The date on the 1928 monument is wrong.

result: Marion meets a larger party; accounts differ on whether any fight took place
other_reading: The NPS timeline says Marion engaged a larger Loyalist group, which retreated, and that a trap at Singleton's Mill failed; the 2010 Clarendon County marker says the British agreed to a staged fight of twenty men each but slipped away overnight, so there was no full battle.
coordinate_basis: HMdb 227896 marker, 33 39.301 N 80 29.724 W (S122); the marker states "according to tradition".
notes: Found by this session; not on Morgan's dagger list. Grey for now. Needs Opus: see SCH09.

result: Loyalist force from Georgia beaten
captured: Morgan reported about 100 killed, 50 wounded and 40 captured among the Loyalists
coordinate_basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121).
notes: Cross-checked: NPS (Washington's dragoons; Loyalists suffered 150 casualties), Wikipedia (Maurer p. 283; O'Neall p. 537; Walker p. 94). No Patriot dead.

result: Tarleton's British regulars defeated
